neighbours.label: 'to' or 'with' after a verb of being forced or brought into a situation (forced to, brought us to)
fire: After the flood, hundreds of families were forced to abandon their homes.
Rising costs may soon bring the company to the edge of bankruptcy.
The prisoners were compelled to work in the mines for years.
His hopes of a medal were dashed with a fall on the final jump.
Without rain, the farmers were driven to sell their cattle cheaply.
The scandal pushed the minister to resign within a week.
The small planets were made to migrate inward by the giant's pull.
Low wages obliged many young people to leave the village.
quiet: After the flood, hundreds of families returned to their homes.
Rising costs were discussed at the company's annual meeting.
The prisoners worked in the mines for years.
His hopes of a medal grew after a clean final jump.
Without rain, the farmers sold their cattle at the spring market.
The scandal was covered by every newspaper within a week.
The small planets moved slowly around the giant star.
Many young people left the village in search of good wages.
